title: Axis Honesty Lab
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Two charts plotting one shared dataset with independently draggable y-axes, a live reader impression under each, an occupancy readout, and a verdict that judges the axis choice against a learner-selected claim.

learningObjectives: Critique chart presentations of identical data.
Judge which axis choices are honest for a stated claim and which mislead.
Construct a defensible presentation for a given audience and claim.
Explain why joining a line across a data gap is misleading regardless of scale.
prerequisites: Chapter 15: line charts and honest axis labelling

keyQuestions: Can two accurate charts of the same data tell opposite stories?
Is truncating the y-axis always dishonest?
What would protect a reader from a misleading axis without changing the data?
What does a line drawn across a six-hour gap assert?
commonMisconceptions: A chart cannot mislead if every plotted point is accurate.
Including zero always makes a chart honest.
Gaps should be joined up so the line is continuous.
assessmentOpportunities: Explains how both charts can be accurate while implying opposite conclusions.
Identifies the dataset where a tight axis is the honest choice.
Names the disclosures that make a truncated axis defensible.
